content: Goldenrod (Solidago) is used for various indications, and its dosing is specific to the condition being treated. It is recommended to drink at least 2 liters of water daily while taking goldenrod. For tea preparation, steep 1 to 2 teaspoons (3 to 5 grams) of the dried herb in 150 mL of boiling water for 5 to 10 minutes, then strain. The tea can be consumed one cup two to four times daily (BID-QID) between meals. Alternatively, a liquid preparation of 0.5 to 1 mL can be taken two to three times daily (BID-TID). Goldenrod is traditionally used for its diuretic, anti-inflammatory, and antispasmodic properties. It has been employed in the management of conditions such as gout, rheumatism, arthritis, eczema, acute pulmonary tuberculosis, diabetes, liver enlargement, hemorrhoids, internal bleeding, allergic rhinitis, asthma, and prostatic hypertrophy. It is also used in irrigation therapy to increase urine flow, which may help treat or prevent inflammatory diseases of the lower urinary tract, urinary calculi, and kidney gravel. However, there is insufficient evidence to confirm its effectiveness for these uses, and further studies are needed. Goldenrod has pharmacodynamic interactions with several diuretics, including amiloride, bendroflumethiazide, bumetanide, chlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, cyclopenthiazide, drospirenone, ethacrynic acid, furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide, indapamide, methyclothiazide, metolazone, spironolactone, torsemide, and triamterene. These interactions result in an increase in the effects of these medications due to pharmacodynamic synergism. However, the clinical significance of these interactions is currently unknown and considered minor. Goldenrod may cause allergic symptoms, particularly in individuals with pollen hypersensitivity. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, there is no specific category assigned, and data is limited. However, it is generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
